Compose a Kernel Specification and a Residual Law

frpp_spec.Rd

Create an experimental FRPP object containing an emhawkes kernel and a separate residual-law object. The result does not inherit from hspec.

Usage

fspec(kernel, residual)
frpp_spec(kernel, residual)
as_fspec(object, name = "legacy")
as_frpp(object, name = "legacy")
as_legacy_hspec(object)

Arguments

kernel

An hspec without residual-distribution slots.

residual

A law created by residual_law.

object

For conversion, an existing FRPP hspec or a frpp_spec. For the legacy adapter, a frpp_spec.

name

A descriptive name for a converted legacy law.

Details

The current model refreshes every dimension's candidate residual after every event in the combined process. It does not retain separate residual clocks. Conversion preserves callback functions and their default bindings without executing them. Captured environments remain references, as in emhawkes. The primary constructor is fspec, matching the hspec naming convention. frpp_spec and as_frpp remain compatibility names. New objects have classes c("fspec", "frpp_spec"); saved objects from the first prototype can still use the old simulation and likelihood methods. The adapter is transitional: it restores the old FRPP representation to use existing public emhawkes operations. It is not a pure Hawkes specification.

Value

frpp_spec and as_frpp return a composition object. as_legacy_hspec returns an hspec carrying the residual callbacks.

See also

residual_law, simulate.frpp_spec

Examples

kernel <- methods::new("hspec", mu = .3, alpha = .2, beta = 1)
law <- residual_law(c(shape = 2, rate = 2), stats::dgamma,
                    stats::pgamma, stats::qgamma, stats::rgamma,
                    name = "Gamma(2,2)")
model <- fspec(kernel, law)
model
#> FRPP specification (fspec)
#> Event types: 1
#> Residual law: Gamma(2,2)
#> Residual candidates refreshed after every global event.
stopifnot(!methods::is(model, "hspec"))
